ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached circuit diagram shows a zener regulator circuit. On the left, the source is labeled Vsource = 15 V. A series resistor labeled Rseries has value 500 Ω and connects from the source to the output node. From that node to ground there is a zener diode labeled Vz = 5.1 V. The load resistor Rload is connected from the same output node to ground, so it is in parallel with the zener diode. Reasoning: The text gives Rload = 1 kΩ. Assuming the zener diode is regulating, the output node voltage is clamped at Vz = 5.1 V. The current through the series resistor is Iseries = (15 − 5.1) / 500 = 9.9 / 500 = 0.0198 A = 19.8 mA. The load current is Iload = 5.1 / 1000 = 0.0051 A = 5.1 mA. By KCL at the output node, the zener current is Izener = Iseries − Iload = 19.8 − 5.1 = 14.7 mA.

method.method_draft: Remove the zener mentally and form the Thevenin equivalent of the rest of the circuit at the zener terminals. From the image/text values, Rseries = 500 Ω, Rload = 1 kΩ, and Vs = 15 V. Compute Vth = 15 × 1000/(500 + 1000) = 10 V and Rth = 500 || 1000 = 333.3 Ω. Since 10 V > 5.1 V, the zener clamps at 5.1 V.
